headline: Approved fundraising to renovate 111 Weaver St. fire house annex and fiscal year 28 budget plan; leave pool policy passed 3-1.
summary: The council approved a leave pool policy by a 3-1 vote, with Councilor Goodrich voting no. It also approved a longevity bonus pay policy, a fundraising campaign to renovate 111 Weaver St., and the fiscal year 28 budget plan and schedule. The council also heard a presentation on Burlington Airport noise mitigation and approved city manager evaluation questions and process.
decisions: Approved the consent agenda, including prior minutes, payroll and bill warrants, and other routine items, 3-0.
Approved the longevity bonus pay policy, 3-0.
Approved the leave pool policy as presented, 3-1, with Councilor Goodrich voting no.
Approved staff conducting a fundraising campaign to renovate 111 Weaver St., 3-0.
Approved the fiscal year 28 budget plan and schedule, with the running question and answer document added to council materials, 3-0.
Approved the city manager evaluation questions and process as presented, 3-0.

Motion by Councilor Turkos to approve the fiscal year 28 budget plan and schedule as presented with the addition that the running question and answer document be added among the materials provided to council as in years past, seconded by Councilor Goodrich. Motion carried 3-0.

VI. Council Reports
Mayor Thomas Renner: The Planning Commission will meet this Thursday at 6:30 PM at City Hall. You 
can also watch online. I encourage folks to check out the update regarding the Planning Commission 
that I put out on Front Porch Forum and other City channels. It is a broader update on the Planning 
Commission, not just the last few meetings. I would like to encourage people to attend those meetings 
either in person or virtually. Thank you to everybody who came out for the Pride event in Winooski last 
Wednesday. It was a really lovely showing once again of our community coming together. Thank you to 
Downtown Winooski for their organizing efforts, particularly their amazing staffer, Sarah who does so 
much work to get these events planned and up and running. Thank you to all of the volunteers as well.  
De
puty Mayor Oakleaf: Safe, Healthy, Connected People and the Housing Commission did not meet 
this month due to the lack of topics for the groups. We plan to have our regular meetings in October so 
keep an eye out for the agendas. The Chittenden Solid Waste District has their full board meeting on 
Wednesday evening at 6:00 PM. You can join online or in person at their office in South Burlington. 
There will be a board education topic on process glass aggregate and then an executive session. No 
other agenda items are planned for the meeting.  
Cou
ncilor Al Turkos: Our next Airport Commission meeting is Wednesday, October 7 at 4 PM. Our next 
Inclusion & Belonging Commission meeting will also take place in October, where we will discuss the 
commission model memo. We are currently finalizing the date and will share that information with the 
community as soon as it is confirmed.  
Wednesday, October 7 is Walk to School Day! We’ll have opportunities for community members to help 
make the morning welcoming, safe, and fun for our students. If you’re interested in volunteering, 
please reach out to me directly. I’d love to have you join us. 
Our most recent community clean-up was held on Saturday, September 12, and I’m already looking 
forward to the next one. We’re planning another clean-up for next month. I’m deeply grateful to 
everyone who came out on September 12, helped make our community a little cleaner, and shared 
their interest in joining us for future clean-ups. These efforts are a great reminder that taking care of 
our community is something we do together. I’m excited to keep building on that momentum. 
Cou
ncilor Elsie Goodrich: The Finance Commission met September 15th, and discussed the Boards, 
Committees, and Commission Structure, after reviewing the August version of the memo from Deputy 
Mayor Oakleaf. Some of the discussion echoed the Municipal Infrastructure Commission comments: 
1. A
 clarification of the purpose, expectations, and direction from City Council and staff, and more
collaboration between Commissions and Council.
2. A need for more action-oriented work, tangible outcomes, and a desire for Commission
recommendations to influence decisions & policies.
3. An appetite for more community engagement and outreach responsibilities.
4. Interest in a "Super Commission" model or combining commissions, with frequent meetings, and
combined “Mega Meetings” and meaningful agendas that include the intersection of Housing,
Infrastructure, and City initiatives with financial matters.
5. And a concern that limiting access to infrequent meetings can inhibit opportunities for feedback and
public engagement.
Th
e commission also had a brief discussion on the Goals & Objectives for Economic Vitality in the 
Economic Development Strategic Plan. While the body of the Commission felt that since they are

VII. City Updates 
 
Elaine Wang, City Manager, gave the following updates: 
Winooski is updating its Master Plan into a new Comprehensive Plan, which will guide the city’s future through 
2027 and beyond. Thank you to everyone who attended our Comprehensive Plan Open Houses and shared 
your feedback this summer. If you couldn’t attend, your input is important, so please take a moment to 
complete the community surveys at winooskivt.gov/plan. There are surveys covering land use, infrastructure, 
economic vitality, and safe, healthy, connected people.  
Everyone is invited to the Main Street Revitalization Ribbon-Cutting Ceremony, which starts at 10 AM on 
September 30, 2026 at the Winooski VFW on Main Street. To read the full press release which includes all of 
the details and summarizes the large amount of work that went into this tremendously important project, 
please visit winooskivt.gov/news.  
Are you a resident with an extra vehicle? Are you a college student, business owner, or employee looking for a 
steady parking option? Need a spot in the parking garage during winter parking bans? Just looking for a place 
to park? The City of Winooski is now offering long-term parking space agreements in the Winooski Parking 
Garage on Cascade Way to individuals or households. Multi-month and month-to-month agreements are 
available – to learn more and ﬁll out the inquiry survey to get started, please visit winooskivt.gov/news.  
The General Election is Tuesday, November 3rd, from 7 AM to 7 PM at the Winooski Senior Center. The 
Vermont Secretary of State will mail ballots to registered and active Winooski voters beginning in October, 
using the address on your voter registration. This is your ballot! Once you receive your ballot, you can return it 
by mail to Winooski City Hall, drop it off at the City Clerk’s Ofﬁce, or bring it to the Winooski Senior Center on 
Election Day. You can check your ballot status and register to vote at vote.vermont.gov. 
Residents are invited to join their friends, families, and neighbors tomorrow for the Landry Park Volunteer 
Cleanup event that takes place tomorrow, Tuesday, September 22, from 4 to 6:30 PM. Volunteers can swing 
by Landry Park to make space for new Community Garden plots or, through our partnership with Fellowship of 
the Wheel, help maintain the mountain bike trails.  
Then, this weekend on Saturday, September 26, enjoy the Memorial Park Bird Walk with the Friends of the 
Winooski River and Trish O’Kane, local ornithologist (meaning someone who studies birds) and educator. Enjoy 
learning more about nature in Winooski and discover Memorial Park - binoculars are provided! 
Learn more about both events at winooskivt.gov/programs.

Minutes: Human Resource Director Jesse Acri gave an overview of the policy, which was presented to  
Council on September 8, 2026. The policy mimics what we already have in place for the two collective 
bargaining units that we have for Public Works and the Police Department. It is for those who have 
been with the city long enough to come off of the step scale and are not eligible for an increase outside 
of the cost-of-living adjustment. It is a way to help preserve institutional knowledge and keep services 
for the city with “familiar faces”.  
 
Motion: Motion to approve the longevity bonus pay policy made by Deputy Mayor Oakleaf and 
seconded by Councilor Turkos. Motion Carried 3-0. 
 
B. Discussion/Approval: Leave Pool Policy - Seeking Approval - Jesse Acri, Human Resources Director 
 
Minutes: Director of Human Resources, Jesse Acri, gave an overview of the policy, which was 
presented to Council on September 8, 2026. The policy was amended after feedback from City Council. 
The proposed policy would establish a city-wide leave pool available to regular year-round employees 
who meet eligibility requirements. Revisions include what types of time off can be donated, clarification 
of eligibility, addressing concerns about negative balances, city staff being able to retain their own 
time, and making sure IRS guidelines are followed. Mayor Renner reiterated that Council wants to make 
sure staff is taking their time off and taking care of themselves. Councilor Goodrich expressed that she 
was uncomfortable with anything other than sick time being included in the policy, and she would be 
interested in talking to the Vermont League of Cities and Towns to get their feedback on a 
compassionate leave policy. She stated she would prefer to look at leave policies in general before 
considering a leave pool. Councilor Turkos stated that she “seconded” what Councilor Goodrich had just 
stated. Finance Director Angela Aldieri provided an overview of donations as well as usage of the pool. 
Further discussion included narrowing the hours that can be donated to only sick leave until the 
Vermont League of Cities and Towns can be consulted and other options can be explored. Finance 
Director Aldieri stated that the sick leave bank is very small compared to other forms of time off based 
on how much is accrued overall. City Manager Wang stated that she would recommend that they 
accept the policy as is and there is no current problem except not having a formal policy in place. There 
are several people who could be impacted soon if there is no policy. If the goal is to make sure no one is 
harmed, it will have the opposite effect. If the policy is passed, other options can be looked at more 
carefully when there is more time.  
 
Motion: Motion by Deputy Mayor Oakleaf to approve the leave policy as presented, seconded by 
Councilor Turkos. Motion carried 3-1, with Mayor Renner, Councilor Turkos and Deputy Mayor Oakleaf 
voting yes, and Councilor Goodrich voting no. 
 
C. Discussion: Burlington Airport (BTV) Noise Mitigation Update - Jazmine Hurley, Housing Initiative 
Director, Nic Longo, Director of Aviation, Larry Lackey, Director of Planning Engineering and 
Sustainability, and Madison Reagan, Environmental Compliance and Project Manager 
 
Minutes: Representatives of the Patrick Leahy Burlington Airport (BTV) provided a presentation 
regarding the status of their soundproofing efforts. Among the items covered were passengers served 
over the last several years, status as second busiest airport in New England in terms of operations, 
and the role of the Vermont National Guard. An overview was given of the history of the noise 
mitigation program including the use and of noise exposure maps and process for updating those 
maps, noise compatibility planning, and the residential sound insulation program. Federal Aviation 
Administration (FAA) Part 150 guidelines were discussed. An overview was given of the components of 
the noise compatibility program including sound insulation, sales assistance and purchase assurance. 
Real time noise monitoring was discussed. An update of statistics for the residential sound insulation

program as it relates to Winooski was provided, with twenty-two units currently in the program. The 
next FAA grant (Phase 6) was discussed along with outreach and eligibility. It was stated that a non-
local company was winning the bids due to the specialized nature of the work involved, but they often 
sub-contract locally. An overview was given of the airport’s efforts to monitor wildlife habitats around 
the airport. It was brought up by Council that the public portal to view the real time noise monitoring 
needs to be more easily accessible on the airport’s website.  
 
Wendy Critchlow of Colchester spoke at the public comment portion of the presentation. She stated 
she lives very close to Winooski and is concerned about the level of noise at her residence. She 
requested someone perform a decibel reading at her house. Nic Longo discussed some of the details 
around contour and noise exposure maps, noise monitors and decibel readings. They will talk offline 
about the concerns that were expressed.  
 
D. Discussion/Approval: Fundraising Campaign for 111 Weaver St. (Fire House Annex) - John Audy, Fire 
Chief 
 
Minutes: Fire Chief John Audy stated this is an effort to furnish the two rooms at 111 Weaver St. for 
full-time staff. This will assist in the purchase of furniture and other necessary items and assist in the 
rigorous cleaning and maintenance involved with the house. City Manager Wang stated that there 
were some questions from individual members of council about soliciting from the general public due 
to current economic conditions. Other general outreach options were included as a way to mitigate the 
possible perception the developer community might infer that there is some kind of “tit for tat” for 
donating. She stated that is the other way around, as it is a large reason why we need the secure 24x7 
staffing. They are already getting something. The Council indicated support for the Fire Department to 
do fundraising, with recognition that there will be directed “asks”. It was also recognized that some in 
the community are facing more difficult economic circumstances. Continuous fundraising was 
discussed rather than one time fundraising, as well as continued engagement of the community. 
Appreciation was expressed for the staff’s willingness to obtain second-hand furniture as well as 
asking for donation of goods.     
 
Motion: Motion by Councilor Turkos to approve staff conduction a fundraising campaign to renovate 
111 Weaver St., seconded by Councilor Goodrich. Motion carried 3-0. 
 
E. Discussion/Approval: Fiscal Year 28 Budget Planning - Angela Aldieri, Finance Director 
 
Minutes: Finance Director Aldieri stated the presentation was a recommendation by staff to follow the 
precedent set in prior years in terms of scheduling. Staff has started meeting on the fiscal year 28 
budget process and will continue to meet until the Council’s first meeting in December. The Council will 
be asked to have a budget goal setting session on October 5th to give staff guidance on what they 
should be presenting. Clarification regarding schedule dates was provided to the Council. City Manager 
Wang gave an overview of the presentation schedule beginning with a high-level presentation and 
then detailed presentations with other staff taking place. It was discussed to continue with a running 
question and answer reference document similar to previous years. The status of language access was 
discussed. City Manager Wang stated that it is still in initial phases of implementation. A new phase is 
being entered into and there needs to be a meeting with the Communications Director to discuss a 
best path forward. Deputy Mayor Oakleaf stated she would appreciate a summary as to the status of 
the language access program and what staff are considering as it relates to the budget season.

Motion: Motion by Councilor Turkos to approve the fiscal year 28 budget plan and schedule as 
presented with the addition that the running question and answer document be added among the 
materials provided to council as in years past, seconded by Councilor Goodrich. Motion carried 3-0. 
 
IX. Proposed Executive Session 
 
A. Discussion: City Manager Evaluation Questions and Process - Elaine Wang, City Manager 
 
Motion: Motion by Deputy Mayor Oakleaf to find that pursuant to state statute 1 V.S.A §313 that 
discussion of the City Manager evaluation and process to the public will put the city at a disadvantage 
and so should be discussed in Executive Session, seconded by Councilor Turkos. Executive session 
entered into at 7:45 PM. 
 
Motion: Motion by Deputy Mayor Oakleaf to come out of Executive Session at 8:01 PM, seconded by 
Councilor Turkos. Motion carried 3-0. 
 
X. Regular Items 
 
A. Discussion/Approval: City Manager Evaluation Questions and Process 
 
Minutes: There was no discussion. 
 
Motion: Motion by Deputy Mayor Oakleaf to approve the questions and process as presented, 
seconded by Councilor Turkos. Motion carried 3-0.  
 
IX. Adjourn 
 
Motion: Motion to adjourn at 8:02 PM by Deputy Mayor Oakleaf, seconded by Councilor Turkos. Motion 
carried 3-0.
